intro.opening: The temples south of the Aswan High Dam are not where they used to be. When Lake Nasser was filled in the late 1960s, several Nubian monuments were saved: cut into blocks, lifted and reassembled on higher ground. On New Kalabsha island, just upstream of the dam, you visit three of them: the Temple of Kalabsha, the rock-cut Temple of Beit el-Wali and the small Roman-period Kiosk of Kertassi.
intro.whyThisOrder: On the island, the guide takes the three structures in sequence. Kalabsha comes first, because it's the largest and the longest visit. Then Beit el-Wali, about twenty minutes for the painted reliefs, and last the Kertassi kiosk at the water's edge for the closing photograph.
fitFor: are already in Aswan and want the quieter UNESCO-rescue chapter that Abu Simbel usually crowds out
want a half day to go with Philae or Abu Simbel
like a short crossing and thin crowds
worthKnowing: This is a shared-departure group tour.
The crossing to the island is by motor boat, roughly fifteen minutes across open water.
The temples are intact in form, but the setting is engineered: a man-made island in a man-made lake, with the dam wall visible to the north.
You spend roughly two to two and a half hours on the island.
intro.closingLine: Half a day on the new island is enough to give them their own chapter.

stops.title: Pickup from your hotel in Aswan
stops.text: A short drive south through the city to the dock just above the High Dam.

stops.title: Motor-boat crossing to New Kalabsha island
stops.text: Roughly fifteen minutes across open water, with the dam wall to one side.

stops.title: The Temple of Kalabsha
stops.text: The first and longest visit. Augustus built it around 30 BC over the foundations of an older Ptolemaic temple, for the Nubian deity Mandulis, a local form of Horus. It's the largest free-standing Nubian temple outside Abu Simbel.

stops.title: The Temple of Beit el-Wali
stops.text: About twenty minutes at a small rock-cut chapel built by Ramses II in the early thirteenth century BC. Its reliefs of his Nubian campaigns keep unusual pigment.

stops.title: The Kiosk of Kertassi
stops.text: What remains of a Roman-period rest-station: four columns and a graceful entablature at the water's edge. This is the stop for the closing photograph.

stops.title: Boat back to the dock and drive to your hotel
stops.text: The boat returns to the dock, then it's a short drive back into central Aswan. Hotel drop-off by early afternoon.

included: A licensed guide in your language (English, Spanish or Japanese)
Morning pickup from your hotel in Aswan, and drop-off back at your hotel
Motor-boat crossing to New Kalabsha island and back
A bottle of water per person
notIncluded: Tipping for your guide: not obligatory, but recommended
options: Pair it with Philae the same afternoon
Ask about lunch in a Nubian village on the way back
Time the boat around your Aswan hotel or your Nile cruise berth
